Strait of Hormuz Status: October 8, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
8 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.51 + 3.71 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 gCaptain, BBC News, and Splash247 report a tanker was struck by multiple projectiles off Qatar's north coast, with casualties among the crew.

02 BNN Bloomberg and Reuters report Iran intends to soon close routes in the Strait of Hormuz it deems unauthorised; US CENTCOM calls Iran's closure claim false.

03 Brent crude stood at $105.51, up 3.71% over 24 hours, as of 15:27 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz conflict has extended its geographic reach: gCaptain, BBC News, and Splash247 report that a tanker was struck by multiple projectiles off the north coast of Qatar, with casualties reported among the crew, signalling that attack risk now reaches beyond the strait itself. BNN Bloomberg also reports that attack risks for tankers are rising as Iran vows to block more Hormuz routes. Separately, BNN Bloomberg and Reuters report that Iran intends to soon close what it regards as unauthorised routes in the strait. An IRGC adviser says the strait stays closed until Iran's demands are met; US CENTCOM calls that closure claim false, leaving the physical transit picture contested. Hellenic Shipping News reports Iran has stepped up attacks on tankers transiting the strait, with nearly 20 commercial ships coming under attack over the past month, threatening a fragile rebound in crude exports from the Persian Gulf. BNN Bloomberg and Reuters, citing the stalled state of US-Iran talks, report that tanker attacks reached a record high last week. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; a multi-day lag is expected given the weekly publication schedule. Brent crude stood at $105.51, up 3.71% over the prior 24 hours, as of 15:27 UTC. Supertanker freight rates have jumped more than eightfold, per International Business Times. The Economic Times reports that the Strait of Hormuz, uranium enrichment, and oil prices are the three issues standing between the United States and Iran in deal negotiations, though no parties to any active talks have been publicly named by both sides. As of 15:20 UTC, 196 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
